Airgas is seeking a Production Supervisor for the night shift of one of our Dry Ice facilities. The Production Supervisor will guide Plant Operators in tasks such as production, packaging of dry ice, shipping preparation, and loading/unloading products in commercial trucks.

Coordinates and guides the safe operation, start-up, and shutdown of the dry ice plant while managing team tasks like production, packaging, and shipping preparation.

Coordinates with the local branch to ensure production resources (labor, materials, and equipment) match production demand.

Communicates operational status on a continual basis to the Plant and Branch Managers.

Interviews and welcomes new production associates to the team, later completing written evaluations and annual reviews.

Mentors, trains, and guides production associates to ensure alignment with Airgas safety, quality, and operational policies.

Manages and monitors supply inventories to ensure that proper materials are on-hand for production needs.

Identifies and facilitates the correction of all safety hazards and quality deficiencies, occasionally operating a forklift to meet production needs.

Works 70% of the time within an unconditioned work space (requiring PPE and protective gloves for handling cold dry ice) and 30% of the time in an office setting.

Remains available for required on-call and shift work.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

70% of the time within an unconditioned work space (i.e. warm in summer, cool in winter). Hazards required the use of personal protective equipment (i.e. hardhat, safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety shoes). Dry ice is extremely cold, and therefore requires that gloves be worn when directly handling dry ice.

30% of the time in an office setting (i.e. desk/computer station.

On-call and shift work required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Essential job function requires occasional lifting and manipulation of dry ice blocks ranging in weight from 5 – 50 pounds each.

________________________Are you a MATCH?

Required Qualifications:

Education & Experience: A High School diploma combined with extensive experience, specifically including three (3) years of supervising 10+ production workers in an industrial setting.

Leadership & Discipline: Strong decision-making skills to enforce company policies, plant procedures, and discipline staff in a fair, professional manner.

Administration & Communication: Very good written/verbal communication for basic reports, plus organizational skills to manage personnel files, time tracking, and inventory.

Math & Computer Literacy: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, email) and higher-level math skills necessary for budgeting and cost control.

Environment & Physical Demands: Ability to work and lead a team safely in a noisy environment with elevated CO_2 vapor, including the physical capability to occasionally lift 5–50 lb. Dry Ice blocks.

Preferred Qualifications:

Advanced Education: An Associate's degree is preferred

Industry Expertise: Prior knowledge of operating specific ice plant machinery (block presses, saws, pelletizers, and valves).

Licensing: An active forklift certification.

The Community Health Worker (CHW) is responsible for helping patients and their families to navigate and access community services, other resources, and adopt healthy behaviors. The CHW supports providers and the Case Managers through an integrated approach to care management and community outreach. As a priority, activities will promote, maintain, and improve the health of patients and their family. CHW provides social support and informal counseling, advocates for individuals and community health needs.

FLSA Status

Non-Exempt

$26.00 - $30.00 per hour

Licensed Clinical Social Worker

Direct Reports

None

Location

Sacramento, CA

Up to 80%

Regular

Schedule

Full-Time (40 hours)

Educating members about ECM services, assisting them with enrollment and serving as the primary liaison between the member and any services they may need.
Support individuals and family as they navigate the health care system and transition to improvement in self-care and health care management.
Responsible for establishing trusting relationships with patients and their families while providing general support and encouragement.
Provide ongoing follow-up, basic motivational interviewing, and goal setting with
patients/families.

Assists members in accessing health-related services and community resources, such as accompaniment to specialist appointments and assistance with enrollment forms.
Facilitates communication between all parties (members, families, colleagues, and community-based organizations) as needed.

Help patients set personal health related goals and attend appointments.
Provide referrals for services to community agencies as appropriate.
Help patients connect with transportation resources and provide appointment reminders in special circumstances.
Exhibit excellent working relations with patients, visitors and staff,
Effectively communicating CHS’ mission.

The platform empowers healthcare providers with digital healthcare products, tools, and services designed to enhance the delivery of care, and improve their patients’ healthcare experience and health outcomes. For more information about the companies, visit; www.well.company, wellclinics.ca

Position Summary

We're looking for a hands-on, deadline-driven coordinator role to drive execution across a fast-moving patient consent program. You'll spend most of your time in the details: chasing owners, updating trackers, running down blockers, and making sure commitments made in meetings happen on the dates promised. You will also be accountable for tracking and optimizing performance metrics across the program by working with key stakeholders throughout the business on strategies, tactics, implementation, and at times change management.

The Mandate

Two Growth Lanes And One Coordination Backbone

Lane 1 — In-Clinic Site Visits & Adoption (71 live clinics): increase consent volume and consistency of the consent workflow at clinics already live, through direct site visits, hands-on troubleshooting, staff engagement, patient communication, and marketing strategies.
Lane 2 — Channel Expansion (in priority order): Direct to Patient Telehealth, Patient
Facing Websites, Online Appointment Booking and other Patient Engagement Channels, and Clinic Network Expansion (i.e. WELL’s Diagnostic Clinics). Expanding consent capture and coordinating pilots with each platform team in that sequence, then scaling rollout.
Coordination backbone: act as the end-to-end coordinator across consent capture, data readiness, and activation requirements for various WELL business units — building a single source of truth, keeping owners and dates current, and escalating blockers fast. This is a “High Agency” position for a results- oriented individual.

What You Will Be Doing

Clinic Adoption

Build and run a clinic-by-clinic adoption plan: identify low-adoption clinics, root-cause why (workflow, training, kiosk friction, patient flow), and drive fixes.
Conduct regular in-clinic site visits and follow-up with clinic managers and on-site engagement staff to keep the consent workflow consistently used, not just installed.
Track and report clinic adoption progress against agreed targets; flag data gaps immediately.
Implement patient communication and marketing techniques designed to optimize adoption.

Channel Expansion

Coordinate pilot scoping and readiness for Direct to Patient Telehealth, Patient Facing Websites, Online Appointment Booking and other Patient Engagement Channels, and Clinic Network Expansion (i.e. WELL’s Diagnostic Clinics).
Support and track existing web/portal consent opportunities to ensure they are actively used, not just available.

Data Readiness & Pipeline Coordination

Track the status of consent linkage, EMR connectivity, and data-pipeline work as it affects downstream usability — this role coordinates across teams, it does not build the pipeline itself.
Maintain visibility into refresh cadence, data quality, and withdrawal handling so downstream teams know what they can rely on and when.
Flag any near-term actions that could create technical, privacy, or patient-experience issues.

Activation Coordination

Interface with research and clinical-commercialization stakeholders to confirm what "usable" data means for each, and track delivery against those requirements.
Interface with the marketing team on marketing-consent needs, keeping marketing and research consent strictly separate in tracking and reporting.
Report on the full funnel: patient exposure through submission, conversion, linkage, and usable activation.

Program Governance

Build and maintain one integrated tracker across capture, data readiness, and activation — owners, dates, dependencies, status, in one place.
Maintain a risk/issue log and a running decision log.
Identify the critical path and top blockers weekly; escalate what needs executive attention rather than letting it stall.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days: Tracker stood up with named owners and dates; clinic and conversion baselines established; first risk/decision log delivered.
First 60 days: Measurable improvement on clinic adoption; first channel pilot ready; first cross-team data-usability report published.
First 90 days: Demonstrated improvement against agreed adoption and conversion targets; additional channel(s) live or launch-ready; clear recommendation on next steps for the role.

Required Qualifications

Proven track record as a program/project coordinator who thrives on execution detail — tracking, chasing, following up, and closing loops.
Comfort operating with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and an aggressive timeline; able to self-direct within a short-term, high-urgency mandate.
Strong stakeholder-management skills across technical, clinical, marketing, and executive audiences.
Fluency with dashboards and spreadsheets (Excel/Sheets or similar); able to build and maintain a clean single source of truth without heavy tooling support.
Excellent, concise written communication — comfortable producing clear status updates and escalation notes for varied audiences.
Demonstrated understanding of the difference between adoption/exposure, submission, conversion, volume, and usability metrics, or ability to learn this funnel quickly

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with patient consent, privacy, or healthcare compliance programs.
Familiarity with clinic operations, EMR systems, or healthcare data pipelines (e.g., Snowflake). Exposure to Tia, Ocean, or similar patient-engagement/booking platforms.
Experience coordinating between clinical research, commercialization, and marketing teams. Prior experience in a short-term, execution-focused "stand this up fast" role.

Maintain availability to work weekends as required by program and operational needs.
Be punctual for scheduled work and use time appropriately.
Perform duties in a conscientious, cooperative manner.
Perform required amount of work in a timely fashion with a minimum of errors.

As a firm passionate about health care, we’re deeply committed to the health and wellness of our own team members. Position Summary

We're looking for a hands-on, deadline-driven coordinator role to drive execution across a fast-moving patient consent program. You'll spend most of your time in the details: chasing owners, updating trackers, running down blockers, and making sure commitments made in meetings happen on the dates promised. You will also be accountable for tracking and optimizing performance metrics across the program by working with key stakeholders throughout the business on strategies, tactics, implementation, and at times change management.

The Mandate

Two Growth Lanes And One Coordination Backbone

Lane 1 — In-Clinic Site Visits & Adoption (71 live clinics): increase consent volume and consistency of the consent workflow at clinics already live, through direct site visits, hands-on troubleshooting, staff engagement, patient communication, and marketing strategies.
Lane 2 — Channel Expansion (in priority order): Direct to Patient Telehealth, Patient
Facing Websites, Online Appointment Booking and other Patient Engagement Channels, and Clinic Network Expansion (i.e. WELL’s Diagnostic Clinics). Expanding consent capture and coordinating pilots with each platform team in that sequence, then scaling rollout.
Coordination backbone: act as the end-to-end coordinator across consent capture, data readiness, and activation requirements for various WELL business units — building a single source of truth, keeping owners and dates current, and escalating blockers fast. This is a “High Agency” position for a results- oriented individual.

What You Will Be Doing

Clinic Adoption

Build and run a clinic-by-clinic adoption plan: identify low-adoption clinics, root-cause why (workflow, training, kiosk friction, patient flow), and drive fixes.
Conduct regular in-clinic site visits and follow-up with clinic managers and on-site engagement staff to keep the consent workflow consistently used, not just installed.
Track and report clinic adoption progress against agreed targets; flag data gaps immediately.
Implement patient communication and marketing techniques designed to optimize adoption.

Channel Expansion

Coordinate pilot scoping and readiness for Direct to Patient Telehealth, Patient Facing Websites, Online Appointment Booking and other Patient Engagement Channels, and Clinic Network Expansion (i.e. WELL’s Diagnostic Clinics).
Support and track existing web/portal consent opportunities to ensure they are actively used, not just available.

Data Readiness & Pipeline Coordination

Track the status of consent linkage, EMR connectivity, and data-pipeline work as it affects downstream usability — this role coordinates across teams, it does not build the pipeline itself.
Maintain visibility into refresh cadence, data quality, and withdrawal handling so downstream teams know what they can rely on and when.
Flag any near-term actions that could create technical, privacy, or patient-experience issues.

Activation Coordination

Interface with research and clinical-commercialization stakeholders to confirm what "usable" data means for each, and track delivery against those requirements.
Interface with the marketing team on marketing-consent needs, keeping marketing and research consent strictly separate in tracking and reporting.
Report on the full funnel: patient exposure through submission, conversion, linkage, and usable activation.

Program Governance

Build and maintain one integrated tracker across capture, data readiness, and activation — owners, dates, dependencies, status, in one place.
Maintain a risk/issue log and a running decision log.
Identify the critical path and top blockers weekly; escalate what needs executive attention rather than letting it stall.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days: Tracker stood up with named owners and dates; clinic and conversion baselines established; first risk/decision log delivered.
First 60 days: Measurable improvement on clinic adoption; first channel pilot ready; first cross-team data-usability report published.
First 90 days: Demonstrated improvement against agreed adoption and conversion targets; additional channel(s) live or launch-ready; clear recommendation on next steps for the role.

Required Qualifications

Proven track record as a program/project coordinator who thrives on execution detail — tracking, chasing, following up, and closing loops.
Comfort operating with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and an aggressive timeline; able to self-direct within a short-term, high-urgency mandate.
Strong stakeholder-management skills across technical, clinical, marketing, and executive audiences.
Fluency with dashboards and spreadsheets (Excel/Sheets or similar); able to build and maintain a clean single source of truth without heavy tooling support.
Excellent, concise written communication — comfortable producing clear status updates and escalation notes for varied audiences.
Demonstrated understanding of the difference between adoption/exposure, submission, conversion, volume, and usability metrics, or ability to learn this funnel quickly

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with patient consent, privacy, or healthcare compliance programs.
Familiarity with clinic operations, EMR systems, or healthcare data pipelines (e.g., Snowflake). Exposure to Tia, Ocean, or similar patient-engagement/booking platforms.
Experience coordinating between clinical research, commercialization, and marketing teams. Prior experience in a short-term, execution-focused "stand this up fast" role.

Company Description

We help job seekers and career changers prepare for and advance in careers with a focus on sustainable, high-growth, high-demand industries. Our committed and well-trained workforce professionals deliver comprehensive workforce solutions at integrated career centers, sector-focused centers and community, and partner sites.

Job Description

The position requires strong stakeholder engagement skills, advanced program coordination abilities, and a high level of expertise in process improvement to enhance operational efficiency and funder satisfaction. In addition to these technical competencies, the role provides clear leadership in guiding initiative teams, directing workflow execution, and ensuring strategic alignment across projects. The position exercises significant supervisory influence, driving program development, providing direction to staff assigned to initiatives, and overseeing key strategic functions that extend well beyond traditional coordinator responsibilities.

Provide day‑to‑day supervision and oversight of staff assigned to special initiatives, ensuring prioritization of tasks, quality of work, and adherence to project goals.
Lead the planning, execution, coordination, and reporting of special initiatives, ensuring staff understand expectations, timelines, and deliverables.
Serve as the primary liaison to employers, schools, community organizations, and partner agencies, representing the project and guiding staff in external engagement activities.
Oversee coordination of logistics, schedules, timelines, and resource needs, delegating tasks appropriately and ensuring timely completion.
Direct the analysis, development, and implementation of process improvements, guiding staff through continuous improvement activities.
Supervise the development and maintenance of SOPs, best practices, and change management strategies, ensuring team compliance and proper training.
Provide training, coaching, and functional guidance to staff to support development, performance, and adherence to program standards.
Ensure staff conduct eligibility screenings, orientations, and Employment Plan development accurately and in alignment with program requirements.
Oversee participant engagement, including identifying barriers to employment and ensuring staff provide appropriate support.
Review and ensure accuracy of supportive service requests, verification activities, order processing, and reconciliation of receipts.
Maintain oversight of case notes and documentation, ensuring staff record timely, accurate, and compliant information in required systems.
Guide the preparation and generation of reports using internal systems and available program data.
Oversee organization and maintenance of the project Share Drive, ensuring policies, procedures, and documents remain current and accessible.
Supervise management of project social media platforms and live chat features, ensuring appropriate and timely communication.
Coordinate team meetings, schedules, and project activities, providing clear communication and follow‑through on action items.
Ensure confidentiality of participant and company information, and promote proper stewardship of company resources.
Perform other supervisory and project‑related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a related field (e.g., Human Services, Education, Business, Public Administration, Workforce Development, or similar).
Minimum 3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in program coordination, workforce development, education services, community engagement, employer relations, or similar fields.
At least 3-5 years of supervisory or lead experience, including providing functional guidance, workflow direction, performance support, or direct supervision of staff.
Experience working with youth programming, externships, transition services, grant‑funded initiatives, or workforce readiness programs.

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
